text.title: Readiness Checklist Core Rules
text.summary: The canonical 10-item checklist as 10 testable rules, plus the gate rule that binds them. Each item is a binary tick with evidence link. Any unticked item blocks the in-progress → done transition. HARD rules — the reviewer cannot waive a conditional item by claiming inapplicability without justification.

rule.statement: All ACs from spec.md have evidence (test id or screenshot reference) linked next to the checkbox.
rule.rationale: An AC without a verifiable artefact is a claim, not a result. The link IS the audit trail.

rule.statement: All tasks moved to tasks/done/. tasks/todo/ and tasks/in-progress/ are empty.
rule.rationale: An unmoved task means work the developer thinks is irrelevant — explicit close-out exposes the assumption.

rule.statement: Commits are granular, follow `type(F0NN-T0N): ≤50 char title`, contain no Co-Authored-By line and no emoji.
rule.rationale: Granular history is the release-notes raw material. Forbidden trailers and emoji break the repo policy hook.

rule.statement: CI is green: lint + typecheck + unit tests all pass on the feature branch.
rule.rationale: Baseline machine check. Skipping it is the cheapest way to ship a regression.

rule.statement: API tests pass — REQUIRED ONLY when the feature touches backend. If ANY file under the backend source tree changed, item 5 (API tests pass) MUST be ticked; the git diff decides, not the developer's assessment of scope.
rule.rationale: Backend surface changes break contracts silently if not contract-tested. Even one line in a serializer can shift a contract. The git diff is the source of truth, not the developer's assessment of scope.

rule.statement: Playwright positive AND negative cases pass — REQUIRED ONLY when the feature has a user-facing flow (page, form, button, command). Item 6 requires AT LEAST one positive test case AND one negative test case per flow.

rationale.source: quality-gates stack-to-gate matrix; user-flows-template pos+neg rule

rule.rationale: Positive only proves the happy path. Negative catches the unsexy edges where regressions hide. Positive only is a smoke test. Negative trumps positive for the boring edges — auth failure, network down, invalid input — which is where users actually break the product.

rule.statement: ui-ux-design.md heuristics reviewed — REQUIRED ONLY when the feature touches UI. If the feature renders or changes any visible UI element, item 7 requires a documented Nielsen 5 + Norman 2 audit in ui-ux-design.md before the box is ticked.
rule.rationale: Heuristic audit catches affordance and feedback bugs before they reach the user. Heuristic audits cost minutes and catch the silent UX regressions that no unit test sees.

rule.statement: project-spec/ delta is drafted in the same PR, OR readiness.md explicitly states "no spec impact" with a one-line reason.
rule.rationale: The same-PR rule from project-spec-structure. The escape hatch is loud on purpose.

rule.statement: Surface coupling reviewed: any new public surface (skill trigger, API path, CLI flag, exported name) has been checked against unrelated surfaces for accidental coupling. For every public surface added or modified by the feature, grep the project for sibling surfaces in the same namespace and document — in readiness.md — that no collision exists OR that the collision is intentional and disambiguated.

rationale.source: F001→F002 incident in the faion plugin

rule.rationale: F001→F002 lesson — two unrelated features collided through skill description overlap. Item makes the review explicit. The collision is invisible at single-PR review and only surfaces at runtime. Forcing the explicit grep moves the check left.

rule.statement: Feature is deployed to the host listed in project-spec/deploy.md (per the deploy-after-feature memory rule).
rule.rationale: Done is "users can use it", not "the merge button was clicked". Closing the loop blocks ship-and-forget.

rule.statement: Any unticked applicable item blocks the in-progress → done transition. Items 5, 6, 7 may be marked not-applicable only with a justification naming what the feature does not touch; the reviewer cannot waive a gate by claiming inapplicability without justification.
rule.rationale: Empty boxes block the transition. Pinning the conditions for items 5, 6, 7 is what stops the reviewer from waiving the gate by claiming inapplicability without justification.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; tick every applicable item with linked evidence and emit readiness.md passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when the feature sits in in-progress/ and the developer claims it is done.

rule.statement: Skip; a sibling methodology (sdd-promotion-gate-checklist, cr-bug-tracking) is the better fit for the lifecycle position, or a precondition is missing.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
